source: Adam pasted both business.adobe.com pages on 2026-11-18; checked by the main session; every quote proven present in the saved paste

claims.claim: Claude Design sends a page into Adobe Experience Manager (ChatGPT fact-check; round one record 6 needed this paste)
claims.what_adobe_says: A marketer finishes a design in Claude Design and uses its 'Send to' feature to push it into Adobe Experience Manager in one click, where it becomes a managed page inside AEM's governance and approval workflows. Adobe's post says 'Adobe Experience Manager' and 'a Claude-designed page'; it does not say which AEM delivery (traditional AEM Publish or Edge Delivery Services), so it maps to AEM Sites as the existing AEM lines do.

quotes.quote: Adobe Experience Manager and Adobe Journey Optimizer are now available as workflow destinations in Claude Design’s new “Send to” export feature.
Customers can push a design from Claude directly into either system with a single click — no download, reconstruction or context-switching required.
Bring a Claude-designed page into Adobe Experience Manager for governed enterprise delivery and optimization.
The design becomes a managed, brand-ready experience, truly streamlining the creation to publication workflow.

prerequisites: Claude Design on the client side
real_limits: Adobe does not say which AEM delivery the page lands in
lead_was_wrong_about: ChatGPT's wording 'for author review' is its own; Adobe says the page enters AEM's governance and approval workflows

claims.claim: Claude Design sends an email into Journey Optimizer as a template (ChatGPT fact-check; round one record 7 needed this paste)
claims.adobe_status: available for email ("now available"); mobile and conversational are "on the roadmap"
claims.what_adobe_says: A marketer builds an email in Claude Design and pushes it into Journey Optimizer as a ready-to-use template, structured for personalization, segmentation and activation. Email only: Adobe says mobile and conversational are on the roadmap, so those are not published.

quotes.quote: For email, the workflow is just as direct and efficient. Claude Design produces an HTML file that Adobe Journey Optimizer (AJO) can use immediately as a template.
push it to Adobe Journey Optimizer as a ready-to-use template. The email arrives structured for personalization, segmentation and activation.
This is a new entry point for email creation inside Adobe Journey Optimizer, with mobile and conversational updates on the roadmap.

prerequisites: Claude Design on the client side

claims.claim: Claude Design sends a design into Adobe Express
claims.what_adobe_says: Adobe says Express is included in the Claude Design launch. Round one found that this hand-off runs through Adobe's connector in Claude, and Adobe's help page for that connector says 'Adobe Express capabilities aren't available to enterprise accounts.' That is a real limit for the tool's enterprise clients, so there is still no Claude line to Adobe Express.

quotes.quote: is also included in the launch, giving creative teams a full end-to-end path from Claude ideation into Adobe’s creative and marketing product suite.

real_limits: Adobe Express capabilities through the Claude connector aren't available to enterprise accounts (helpx, round one)

claims.claim: Experience Manager, Journey Optimizer, Customer Journey Analytics and Workfront are available connectors in Claude
claims.kind: ready-made by Adobe, an admin switches it on
claims.what_adobe_says: Adobe's own post lists Experience Manager, Journey Optimizer, Customer Journey Analytics, Workfront and the Adobe Marketing Agent as available connectors in Claude. It backs the Claude lines to those four products, Journey Optimizer included (which round one wrongly left out as beta). The Adobe Marketing Agent is not a product in the tool, and this page does not say what it became.

quotes.quote: and the Adobe Marketing Agent are all available Connectors in Claude.

prerequisites: An admin approves the connector in Claude

claims.claim: Adobe Commerce creates product feeds for ChatGPT shopping (round one record 43 needed this paste)
claims.what_adobe_says: The page says Commerce generates channel-ready product feeds and helps products surface across LLMs, search engines, marketplaces and ad channels. It never names ChatGPT, so there is no ChatGPT line from it.

quotes.quote: Adobe Commerce helps ensure your products are surfaced and recommended across LLMs, search engines, marketplaces, and digital advertising channels.
Automatically generate and maintain channel-ready product feeds aligned with destination requirements, reducing manual work and time to publish.

lead_was_wrong_about: The page does not name ChatGPT or OpenAI shopping

claims.claim: Adobe Commerce supports OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)
claims.adobe_status: the page says both 'our commitment to supporting' and 'supports'
claims.what_adobe_says: Adobe's page says Commerce supports Google's and OpenAI's agent shopping protocols, so agents can read products, prices and stock and complete a purchase for the shopper. It names OpenAI's protocol, not ChatGPT, and its main text calls it a 'commitment to supporting'. A ChatGPT line would say more than Adobe does; it belongs with Commerce's own capabilities, for Adam to weigh.

quotes.quote: Adobe Commerce supports both the Unified Commerce Protocol (UCP) from Google and Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) from OpenAI.
This allows agents to securely access product data, check availability and pricing, and complete transactions on the customer’s behalf.
our commitment to supporting new agentic commerce protocols including Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)

real_limits: Adobe names the protocol, not ChatGPT
lead_was_wrong_about: The page spells Google's protocol two ways (Universal and Unified)

claims.claim: Adobe Commerce Storefront server lets any AI assistant shop the client's live store (round one record 78: Experience League marks it 'coming soon')
claims.adobe_status: this page describes it in the present tense; Experience League says 'This feature is coming soon and is subject to change.'
claims.what_adobe_says: A client's developers connect any compatible AI assistant or agent to the live store through Adobe's Commerce Storefront server: search the catalog, read real-time prices and stock, manage the cart and complete checkout. Adobe names no assistant, so it is not a line to the ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot box; it is a Commerce build a partner could sell. Adam's Nov 12 rule ('will be released ... they're going to come') covers a feature marked coming soon.

quotes.quote: The Adobe Commerce Storefront MCP (Model Context Protocol) server gives developers direct access to your live Commerce data and services.
Connect Adobe Commerce to any MCP-compatible assistant or platform, without building custom point-to-point integrations.

The Adobe Commerce Storefront MCP server exposes tools that agents can use to search your product catalog, retrieve real-time pricing and inventory, manage cart contents, and complete checkout — all without requiring custom point-to-point integrations.
This means any compatible AI assistant or agent can deliver accurate, on-brand shopping experiences powered by your actual store data.

lead_was_wrong_about: Round one called it 'not released'; this page describes it in the present tense
